passage: 'As researchers, we compute a ratio-a numerator divided by a denominator-to compute a proportion for some biological response or to derive some standardized variable.' 'only if the relationship between numerator and denominator is a straight line through the origin will the ratio be meaningful' (abstract, Europe PMC).
faulty: Paired t test on the within-subject difference of the ratios force_drug/area_drug - force_vehicle/area_vehicle; criterion: positive mean difference with two-sided p < 0.05.
fixed: Paired analysis of covariance: regress force_drug - force_vehicle on area_drug - area_vehicle with an intercept; the criterion is that the intercept (the adjusted mean paired difference) is positive with two-sided p < 0.05.
estimand: Faulty: mean paired difference in force per unit area, which includes the session difference in area. Fixed: mean paired difference in force at equal area.
model_family: Within-subject linear model force_c = alpha_i + b*area_c + delta*[drug] + e with Gaussian e and non-zero subject intercepts (the source's point: lines not through the origin); fixed for both twins.
sizes_note: Source states no sample size (abstract only). 30 subjects is a realistic crossover study; the check is a single regression. Size dependence: not stated.
exploited_structure: The session (drug or vehicle) varies with the measured area in that session, and force is not proportional to area, so per-area force differs between sessions without a drug effect.

structure_statistic.note_value_source: source states none: the abstract gives no figure; 0.5 is a moderate standardised mean difference in area between sessions (an assumed value)

notes: RESERVE (CUR13 reserve). 'mean' family (paired), paired structure with the session on separate keys. Differs from B3B-03 and B3B-04 by data structure (paired design) and statistic (paired difference).
